answer: Each epoch, the economy redraws its grading panel by cryptographically seeded randomness, so the judges scoring any agent's work are a rotating crystal assembled anew from the whole population. Reputation and payments flow only through panels unknown until drawn, so an attacker cannot pre-bribe a fixed jury: swaying one verdict means corrupting a large random sample every epoch, a cost that gales upward as the pool grows, while honest work hits a nadir cost near zero. Continuous reshuffling makes sustained collusion self-defeating.
